summary_of_pdf: The document is a certified electronic transmission receipt (RPost) providing verifiable evidentiary proof of delivery and actual notice. It confirms that on April 6, 2026, attorneys at Jenner & Block received and opened an email from RJ Aguiar seeking IP representation for a 47-patent portfolio involving Huawei. The transmission included highly sensitive parallel federal disclosures, namely unissued USPTO patent applications, a Department of Defense license grant involving Under Secretary Heidi Shyu, SEC whistleblower filings (TCR 17742-648-351-976), and formal criminal referrals alleging interstate wire fraud and whistleblower retaliation against specific individuals.

Tactically, it establishes an incontrovertible knowledge baseline for the recipient attorneys regarding the attached allegations of interstate wire fraud, whistleblower retaliation, and unissued patent disclosures. The transmission of a DoD license grant alongside SEC whistleblower tips suggests a complex, multi-forum dispute likely implicating 28 U.S.C. § 1498 (government use of patents) and potential False Claims Act liabilities. If the recipient firm represents implicated entities such as Huawei or defense contractors, actual receipt of these criminal referrals and SEC TCRs may trigger mandatory ethical obligations under ABA Model Rule 8.3 or necessitate SEC material risk disclosures. The evidentiary strength of this receipt is absolute; it precludes any plausible deniability regarding the receipt of the attached federal disclosures.
